titles.original_title: 40 Years in the Making: The Magic Music Movie
titles.plot: Filmmaker Lee Aronsohn examines the storied history of the 1970s Colorado jam band Magic Music.

titles.title: 9500 Liberty
titles.plot: In 2007, conservative blogger Greg Letiecq and local politician Corey A. Stewart push through a crackdown on illegal immigrants in Virginia's Prince William County, leading to a local ordinance that allows the police to stop and question anyone who might be an illegal immigrant. When its backers go too far with their heavy-handed tactics, and the ordinance almost immediately contributes to an economic decline of the county, previously silent members of the community make their voices heard.

titles.title: A Family Affair
titles.plot: On his 30th birthday, a man receives an invitation from his grandmother to visit her in South Africa. Although she has been estranged from his family for decades, he decides to go and is shocked when she makes an unexpected confession.

titles.title: American Interior
titles.plot: Welsh musician Gruff Rhys films his latest road trip.

titles.title: Andy Warhol: A Documentary Film
titles.plot: Rare archival film footage and interviews illustrate filmmaker Ric Burns' tribute to art-world icon Andy Warhol. Much of the material Burns uses was shot by Warhol himself during his heydey in the 1960s and '70s. Interviews include art dealer Irving Blum, Warhol's brother John, Paul Morrissey and art critic Dave Hickey.

titles.title: Bare
titles.plot: Eleven naked men audition, rehearse and perform for the premiere of master Belgian choreographer Thierry Smits’s new contemporary dance piece Anima Ardens. Mixing intimate rehearsal footage with extensive and breathtaking dance sequences, BARE follows the choreographer and his team as they work to explore difficult, often taboo subjects through nudity and dance. In this bold exploration of artistic conflict, gender, and sexuality the one constant is the conceit that the body is the last bastion of personal freedom.

titles.title: Be Natural: The Untold Story of Alice Guy-Blaché
titles.original_title: Be Natural: The Untold Story of Alice Guy-Blaché
titles.plot: The life and work of the first female film director.

Be Natural: The Untold Story of Alice Guy-Blaché (2018)

titles.title: Best Worst Movie
titles.plot: This documentary reviews the making of the film "Troll 2" from the perspective of its former child actor star, Michael Stephenson. In 1989, a group of actors and an Italian production crew join forces to produce a slice of unwitting cinematic history. Stephenson and those involved with the ill-fated sequel tell the story of Italian director Claudio Fragasso's B-movie classic, among them the Alabama dentist who became a cult star because of his famous, immortal line.

titles.title: Beuys
titles.plot: Filmmaker Andres Veiel details the life and work of the 20th-century German sculptor and performance artist Joseph Beuys.

titles.title: Blue Carbon: Nature's Hidden Power
titles.plot: DJ and marine toxicologist Jayda G embarks on a global journey to investigate a powerful ally in the battle to slow climate change, blue carbon ecosystems. They explore their potential to absorb carbon dioxide and enhance food security.

titles.title: Bobby Fischer Against the World
titles.plot: Liz Garbus examines the tragic and bizarre life of the late chess master from his troubled childhood through his rise to fame and his life as a fugitive.

titles.title: Bones Brigade: An Autobiography
titles.plot: Filmmaker Stacy Peralta looks back on his own career as a skateboarder and as manager of a talented team of skateboarders.

titles.title: Botero
titles.plot: Filmmaker Don Millar examines the life and works of Colombian artist and sculptor Fernando Botero.

titles.title: Boxing Gym
titles.plot: The veteran award-winning documentary filmmaker Frederick Wiseman turns his lens on the world of boxing, specifically on a gym in Austin, Texas. Unobtrusively recording the simple comings and goings at the facility, Wiseman documents daily life at the gym, its many patrons, their routines and its owner, Richard Lord. The film forgoes techniques common to modern documentaries -- talking-head interviews, reenactments, etc. -- in favor of a low-key approach.

titles.title: Cameraperson
titles.plot: Cinematographer Kirsten Johnson exposes her many years behind the camera through a memoir made up of decades of footage shot all over the world.

titles.title: The Fall of Fujimori
titles.plot: Filmmaker Ellen Perry examines the 10-year reign of Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori.

titles.title: Fast, Cheap & Out of Control
titles.plot: In this documentary by Errol Morris, four men with unique vocations are interviewed. There's Dave Hoover, a lion tamer; George Mendonça, a topiary gardener; Ray Mendez, a hairless mole rat expert; and Rodney Brooks, a robotics designer. Using a special camera called the Interrotron, each of these men is able to talk about his obsession seemingly directly to the audience, while Morris intercuts the interviews with stock footage and movie clips that are used to draw connections between them all.

titles.title: Fatal Assistance
titles.plot: Filmmaker Raoul Peck looks at failed efforts to rebuild post-earthquake Haiti, including the disclosure that much of the money pledge to Haiti was either never disbursed or was not applied to reconstruction efforts.

titles.title: Fightville
titles.plot: Filmmakers Michael Tucker and Petra Epperlein turn a spotlight on mixed martial arts and the lives of several Lousiana-based fighters.

titles.title: Frank and Ollie
titles.plot: Legendary Walt Disney animators Frank Thomas and Ollie Johnston helped create the studio's signature style. In this documentary, the pair look back on their pioneering work on such children's classics as "Lady and the Tramp," "Bambi" and "Pinocchio." Over their decades-long careers, Frank and Ollie remained not only close collaborators but inseparable friends; that's clear enough as the duo fondly recall their time together bringing drawings to life.

titles.title: Gay Sex in the '70s
titles.plot: This documentary explores the birth of the gay pride movement in New York after the Stonewall riots of 1969 and the sexual freedom that resulted. It touches on many aspects of gay culture in the 1970s, including music, drugs and art, followed by the devastating impact that the onset of AIDS had on the homosexual community. Told through several interviews and archival material, it paints a picture of solidarity and positivity while exploring the sexuality of a relatively new movement.

titles.title: Girls Can't Surf
titles.plot: It's the 1980s and the world of professional surfing is a circus of fluoro colours, peroxide hair and radical male egos. GIRLS CAN'T SURF follows the journey of a band of renegade surfers who took on the male-dominated professional surfing world to achieve equality and change the sport forever.

titles.title: Hot Girls Wanted
titles.plot: Filmmakers Jill Bauer and Ronna Gradus shed light on Florida's amateur porn industry through the experiences of five young women in the business.

titles.title: Inay
titles.plot: With the desire to help answer unresolved questions and heal lingering wounds, Inay investigates the flawed immigration pathways between the Philippines and Canada that kept so many Filipino children from their mothers.

titles.title: Inconvenient Indian
titles.plot: Exploring the ongoing cultural colonization of Indigenous peoples in North America and how modern colonization has focused on Indigenous history, culture, and traditions rather than the forceful colonization of the past.

titles.title: InRealLife
titles.plot: Filmmaker Beeban Kidron journeys from the bedrooms of British teenagers to Silicon Valley to see the Internet's effects on children.

titles.title: Laddie: The Man Behind the Movies
titles.original_title: Laddie: The Man Behind the Movies
titles.plot: Alan Ladd Jr. oversees production of some of the most popular movies of all time, including "Star Wars," "Alien," "Blade Runner," "Police Academy" and "Braveheart."

titles.title: Life 2.0
titles.plot: Filmmaker Jason Spingarn-Koff delves into the online world known as Second Life, where people live alternate lives through the avatars they create.

titles.title: At the Edge of the World
titles.original_title: At the Edge of the World
titles.plot: Volunteer activists led by Greenpeace's Paul Watson set sail for the south Antarctic Ocean to protect whales from Japanese hunters.

images.caption: At the Edge of the World (2008)

titles.title: Lives Well Lived
titles.plot: Filmmaker Sky Bergman celebrates the wit and wisdom of 40 adults who are 75 to 100 years old and living their lives to the fullest.

titles.title: Love and Diane
titles.plot: In this unflinching documentary, formerly homeless ex-crack addict Diane Hazzard struggles to prove, both to her six children and to the child welfare bureaucracy of New York City, that she has cleaned up her act and is a fit and caring mother. Meanwhile, Diane's HIV-positive daughter, Love Hinson, has just given birth to her own son, Donyaeh, and struggles to balance the needs of her child with both her own poor mental and physical health and her fractious relationship with her mother, Diane.

titles.title: Marcel Duchamp: The Art of the Possible
titles.original_title: Marcel Duchamp: The Art of the Possible
titles.plot: The life, philosophy and impact of one of the most influential early 20th-century modernists, Marcel Duchamp.

images.caption: Marcel Duchamp: The Art of the Possible (2020)

titles.title: Meru
titles.plot: Three elite climbers fight through obsession and loss as they struggle to climb Mount Meru.

titles.title: Mr. Gaga
titles.plot: Footage of intimate rehearsals and breathtaking dance sequences highlight the life and career of Ohad Naharin, choreographer and artistic director of the Batsheva Dance Company.

titles.title: Nureyev: Lifting the Curtain
titles.plot: Filmmakers Jacqui and David Morris trace the life of Rudolf Nureyev, the Russian dancer who became a cultural icon.

titles.title: Off the Rails
titles.plot: The life of Darius McCollum, a man whose obsession with mass transit has landed him in jail 32 times for impersonating drivers, conductors, token booth clerks, and track repairmen.

titles.title: One Mile Away
titles.plot: Filmmaker Penny Woolcock returns to Birmingham to help feuding gangs end fighting that has raged for over 30 years.

titles.title: Paradise Lost 3: Purgatory
titles.plot: New DNA evidence sheds light on the case of the West Memphis 3, a trio of men who were convicted in 1994 of murdering three suburban Arkansas Cub Scouts.

titles.title: Photographic Memory
titles.plot: Filmmaker Ross McElwee returns to a seaside town in France where he spent time in his younger days, and reconnects with a former sweetheart.

titles.title: Richland
titles.plot:
A U.S. nuclear company town stakes its identity on its little-known atomic origin story in
this timely examination of the habits of thought that normalize the extraordinary
violence of the past.

titles.title: Running With Beto
titles.plot: Filmmaker David Modigliani's behind-the-scenes look at Beto O'Rourke's breakaway campaign that was designed to unseat Ted Cruz in the U.S. Senate.

titles.title: Served Like a Girl
titles.plot: Five female veterans who have endured unimaginable trauma in service create a shared sisterhood to help the rising number of homeless female veterans.

titles.title: Something's Gonna Live
titles.plot: Despite the criticisms leveled against it, the old Hollywood studio system produced many classic films and nurtured the careers of some of moviedom's top artists. Documentarian Daniel Raim turns the camera on several men who spent a lifetime behind it, among them production designer Robert Boyle, cinematographer Haskell Wexler and illustrator Harold Michelson. The group reminisce about their careers and the many well-known and celebrated movies they worked on.

titles.title: Sorry/Not Sorry
titles.plot: An inside look at Louis CK's public downfall and surprising return to the spotlight. Featuring interviews with women who spoke up about his sexual misconduct, New York Times journalists who broke the story, and fellow comedians such as Michael Ian Black, Michael Schur, and Aida Rodriguez. Examines cancel culture and the legacy of the #MeToo movement. A New York Times production.

titles.title: Terms and Conditions May Apply
titles.plot: Filmmaker Cullen Hoback exposes the erosion of online privacy and what information governments and corporations are legally taking from citizens each day.

titles.title: The Art of Political Murder
titles.plot: An investigation into the truth behind the murder of Guatemalan Bishop Juan Gerardi, who was killed in 1998 just days after trying to hold the country's military accountable for the atrocities committed during its civil war.

titles.title: The House I Live In
titles.plot: The death of his housekeeper's son inspires filmmaker Eugene Jarecki to add up the true cost of America's losing war on drugs.

titles.title: The Incomparable Rose Hartman
titles.plot: The life and career of photographer Rose Hartman.

titles.title: The Insufferable Groo
titles.plot: Filmmaker Stephen Groo tries to recruit Jack Black to be in his latest film.

titles.title: The Last Dalai Lama?
titles.plot: A portrait of the 14th Dalai Lama, featuring interviews with his family and the people he has inspired since his exile from Tibet in 1959.

titles.title: The Pinochet Case
titles.plot: Augusto Pinochet, who ruled Chile from the early 1970s through 1990, is the focus of this documentary. South American filmmaker Patricio Guzmán, who himself was forced to leave Chile after Pinochet rose to power, chronicles the collapse of Pinochet's violent and corrupt reign. Guzmán interviews various people who were tortured during the dictator's regime and aims to make the case that a South American court ultimately threw out -- that Pinochet was indeed a war criminal.

titles.title: The Spy Behind Home Plate
titles.plot: Morris Moe Berg was an enigmatic and brilliant Jewish baseball player turned spy. Berg caught and fielded in the major leagues during baseball's Golden Age in the 1920s and 1930s, but very few people know that Berg also worked for the Office of Strategic Services (OSS), spying in Europe and playing a prominent role in America's efforts to undermine the German atomic bomb program during WWII.

trailer.title: The Spy Behind Home Plate: Trailer 1

titles.title: The Swell Season
titles.plot: Oscar-winning musicians Glen Hansard and Markéta Irglová embark on a world tour, but the pressures of touring and performing threaten their offstage romantic relationship.

titles.title: The Truth vs. Alex Jones: Trailer
titles.original_title: The Truth vs. Alex Jones: Trailer
titles.plot: A look at the "The Truth vs. Alex Jones," about the landmark defamation trials brought by Sandy Hook parents against Alex Jones.

titles.title: The Year of the Yao
titles.plot: This documentary chronicles Yao Ming's first year of playing in the National Basketball Association. When Ming signs with the Houston Rockets, he becomes the first player from China to play in the NBA, a feat that makes him immensely popular in his homeland. However, the style of play in the league is vastly different from that in China, and Yao initially struggles. As he becomes more familiar with his teammates and the American culture, however, Yao starts to excel on the court.

titles.title: Top Rider
titles.plot: Exploring the unique culture of motocross in Bermuda and the challenges faced by riders striving to make a name for themselves from the remote island.

titles.title: Unmasking Jihadi John: Anatomy Of A Terrorist
titles.original_title: Unmasking Jihadi John: Anatomy Of A Terrorist
titles.plot: The inside story of Mohammed Emwazi's journey from being an ordinary London boy to becoming terrorist 'Jihadi John', and the intelligence operatives' attempts to catch him.

titles.title: Unmistaken Child
titles.plot: Young monk Tenzin Zopa has spent most of his life studying at the feet of the esteemed Geshe Lama Konchog. When the older man dies after a long, influential life, Tenzin is assigned to find his teacher's reincarnated soul. Tenzin journeys throughout Nepal, from one small village to another, in search of the child in whom Konchog's spirit has come to reside. This documentary charts Tenzin's arduous, emotional quest, a task that will be judged a success or failure by the Dalai Lama himself.

titles.title: Vanish: Disappearing Icons of a Rural America
titles.original_title: Vanish: Disappearing Icons of a Rural America
titles.plot: The "visual preservation" adventures of fine art photographer, Jim Westphalen.

images.caption: Vanish: Disappearing Icons of a Rural America (2024)

titles.title: You've Been Trumped
titles.plot: Scottish landowners go head-to-head with billionaire Donald Trump to prevent construction of a golf resort on an environmentally sensitive stretch of coastline.
